_comment: Conformance vectors for the forge-ci pipeline schema.
Every forge-ci implementation reads THIS file. A vector in invalid must
fail, and the reported error must contain the substring in error.
Schema alone cannot check a cross reference. An alias that names nothing,
or names an engine of the wrong port, is a semantic check the validator
must perform. Those vectors are marked semantic true.

valid.why: a release is a substage naming an artifact engine, beside the substages that build. It runs no target, and what it must not touch is its engine's own business: ignoreRepos in the spec keeps a repo the pipeline writes every run out of the tag set. Stage order is what keeps a publish behind a green build, the same tool that orders everything else.
a repo may declare what must be built before it, and a stage or substage may carry the words a person reads instead of only an identifier.
one repo, one engine, one stage. The smallest thing that runs.
repos is optional. A pipeline with none is valid and its revision is the pipeline file.
a stage fans out. Substages carry user params that forge-ci never interprets.
alias:// resolves as well as forge://, matching forge.
one number per factory: the prefix namespaces the tag, the strategy picks the bump, the cap holds a factory that is not ready for v1, and the vocabulary is whatever the team writes.
no versioning at all is the default every factory uses: no prefix, the patch bump, no cap. Behaviour is exactly what it was before the block existed.
sync on a substage converges the workspace - manifests, then the dependency closure - before its targets run.
an artifact engine that names no ignoreRepos publishes every repo the revision pinned, which is what a factory that owns all its members wants.
unmatched: error enforces the vocabulary: a subject no list claims fails the run before anything builds, so a convention nobody checks becomes one the pipeline checks.
ignorePaths names what never releases; a release set that moved only under them converges without a release.
the self reconcile commit prefix is the factory's to choose; the default is forge-ci:, and a prefix a semantic list also names scores by that list.

invalid.why: a pipeline with no stages does nothing and is almost certainly a mistake.
the go:// scheme is removed. A migration must not fail silently: the error names forge://.
only forge:// and alias:// resolve. Matching forge, anything else is a hard error.
the port list is closed. A typo must not silently create a new port.
aliases are lowercase kebab-case, matching forge enum values.
a target that names no work is meaningless.
forge silently drops unknown keys. forge-ci must not. A typo in a pipeline is a bug you want reported.
state must name an engine that exists.
state must name an engine whose type is state, not merely any engine.
a substage runs on a compute engine. Naming a state engine there is a bug.
a gate must name a gate engine.
two engines with one alias makes every reference ambiguous.
a substage must name a declared target.
a target that names a repo outside repos would run nowhere.
an engine must name a declared manager.
there is no door to type a version into. A version is derived or it is nothing, so it can never be re-pointed at a release that already exists.
a strategy nobody implements would silently fall back to the patch bump, and the operator would never learn their choice did nothing.
a cap on the patch would stop the only bump that always works, so a factory carrying one could never release again.
an unmatched level nothing scores would make every unrecognised subject score whatever the fallback happens to be.
a typo in the versioning block is a bug you want reported, not swallowed. forge-ci rejects unknown keys and forge does not.

a multi-repo workspace builds against generated manifests, so a pipeline that never converges them is building what nobody wrote. JSON Schema cannot count repos against substages, so the validator does.

a release is a substage naming an artifact engine, like anything else a stage does. The stage key it used to hang off is gone, and a pipeline still carrying it is reported rather than silently ignored.
the revision is minted before the first stage runs, so no stage declares it. A pipeline still carrying the key is reported rather than silently ignored.

an artifact substage publishes what the stages before it built; it runs nothing. Targets on one would be read by nobody, and a key nobody reads is a lie about what the pipeline does. Which port the engine implements is a cross reference, so the rule is semantic.
a compute substage with nothing to run is a substage that does nothing. The schema cannot require the key, because an artifact substage must not carry it, so the rule is semantic.

an artifact engine told to leave out a repo the factory does not hold is a typo that would silently tag one repo more than intended. The engine cannot catch it - it never learns the factory's members - so the pipeline validator does.
a repeated name is a copy-paste error worth reporting rather than deduplicating in silence.
one pattern typed as a string would be read as a list of characters or silently dropped; a list is the only shape.
a blank prefix would make every commit read as a self reconcile; the schema cannot see whitespace, so forge-ci refuses it.
